title: Northgate Protect Complete Monthly: Monthly Billing, Declined Fees and Lapse
content:
Northgate Protect Complete Monthly is charged its monthly fee on the enrollment date and then on the same calendar day of each month, falling back to the last day of a shorter month, to the payment method on the plan; a fee charged to a Northgate Card posts there as a purchase. When a monthly fee is declined the plan stays active but no claim is accepted while the fee is unpaid, since the tier accepts no claims during the grace period. A Complete Monthly plan lapses only when a declined monthly fee is still unpaid after the declined attempt date plus the tier's payment grace days. Calendar days are added to the date of the first declined attempt for that month, the day after it being day 1, and the plan lapses on the day after the last grace day. Paying the fee within the grace period restores claims from the payment date, and incidents during the unpaid days are not covered. One-time plans are charged once at purchase and are never charged again.

## Billing dates, worked

| Hypothetical enrollment day | Following fee dates |
|---|---|
| 12 March | 12 April, 12 May and so on |
| 31 January | 28 February (29 February in a leap year), then 31 March |

## Grace and lapse, worked

*Hypothetical, with a 15-day grace period:* the first declined attempt for a month is on 10 May. Day 1 is 11 May and day 15, the last grace day, is 25 May.

| Fee still unpaid on | Plan position |
|---|---|
| 25 May | Active, claims not accepted |
| 26 May | Lapses on this day |

If the fee is paid on 20 May, claims are accepted again from 20 May, and an incident on 15 May, during the unpaid days, is not covered.

## Points of judgement

- The clock runs from the first declined attempt for that month, as the plan's billing records show it, not from a later retry.
- A declined fee alone never ends the plan; only the passing of the grace days with the fee unpaid does.
